mission: Capture batch count means 'up to' (owner 2026-10-19 13:02Z). enqueue-capture-batch judged only the oldest 2 * count candidates, so a smaller count judged fewer and found fewer eligible (MEASURED: 12 of 100 at count 50, 9 of 24 at count 12, dry run 39255746139), and it refused whenever eligible < count, dropping the guard counts. Now every bounded ambiguous family is planned, the shared-print guard runs in plan order, the batch is min(count, eligible), it refuses only when nothing is eligible (with the breakdown kept), and an apply refuses only on a SHA-256 mismatch. A new read-only runbook capture-batch-preview (ops-readonly, no approval) gives the full exclusion breakdown (reviewed, blocked, captured, queued, exact now per rule, resolved since, unbounded, no release, first failed guard), the batch, its SHA-256 and storage fit. No application, collector or schema change; no capture is dispatched by this PR.

impacts.reason: enqueue-capture-batch (ops-write, owner-gated, collector-affecting on apply) plans every uncaptured bounded ambiguous family instead of the first 2 * count, applies the shared-print guard greedily in plan order, takes min(count, eligible), and refuses only on zero eligible; apply still re-plans and refuses on a different SHA-256. Every #116 guard and the #116 tool's checks are unchanged. replan.finish is split so its summary is reusable; enqueue-remaining-50 behaves as before. New read runbook capture-batch-preview: the same plan over the read-only ops session (default_transaction_read_only=on), writes nothing.
Adds capture-batch-preview to the runbook choice list and an optional count input passed only to it. No permission, secret, environment or trigger change.

Shortlist keeps every bounded family with a reason per drop; greedy shared-print guard; stopping at count gives the same batch and SHA as judging all; count means up to (9 eligible of 12 requested gives 9); refusal only on zero eligible keeps the breakdown; apply refuses on a SHA mismatch and passes on the dry run's SHA; population SQL read-only on the real schema; preview is a read runbook.
Documents the up-to-N semantics, the exclusion reasons and capture-batch-preview.
